newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend gains, seen down on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend gains, seen down on Thursday.

text.p: Polish shares rose for the second day running on Wednesday but analysts said the strong post- price-fixing selling signalled a profit-taking fall on Thursday after recent sharp small-cap price rises.
The overall market has flattened out over the past week after the previous 38-percent, large-cap driven surge that started in mid-December.

"There have been big gains...and that's likey what led to selling today (after price fixing and in live trade) because the risk increases when firms grow so many times by the daily maximum," said Cezary Markiewicz of Bank Gdanski brokerage.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.7 percent to 18,251.3 points and turnover rose 28.2 percent to 250.4 million zlotys ($82.3 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 61 to 17 with 10 stocks flat.

On Wednesday small-cap non-ferrous metals smelter Olawa, builders Espebepe and Remak, furniture Swarzedz and wood firm Paged all rose between 9.3 and 10 percent, with Espebepe's post-price-fixing buying strong enough to reduce players' bids.
Analysts said garment maker Prochnik would likely rise on Thursday after an owner's public tender call on Tuesday.
Prochnik trade was suspended on Wednesday, the day after National Investment Fund No.12 announced it would buy 343,501 shares at 11 zlotys ($3.6), with the stock currently quoted at 9.7 ($3.2).
NFI units fell 0.6 percent in 35.2-million-zloty ($11.6 million) trade at the regular session and fell 1.2 percent in 24.7-million-zloty ($8.1 million) continuous trade.

Analysts termed a good sign the Wednesday statement by new Finance Mininster Marek Belka that capital gains taxes on individuals would remain tax-free to 2000, but analysts did not expect a significant short-term effect on stock prices.
